events.text: I need the lab's rules for running experiments and publishing contributions before choosing a direction, so I'll read the guide and the data layout first.
The guide's example was truncated, so I need the schema, the baseline definitions, and the dataset READMEs before picking a direction.
The baseline is one-hot position×amino acid with ridge regression. Before designing a model I need its exact code, the test-profile fields in the schema, and the DOMAIN file.

The baseline is one-hot position×amino-acid ridge, which ignores position-level signal in a way a target encoding would capture. Before writing the model, I need the part of the guide that was truncated (how `prediction` tests name datasets and inputs), plus the test schema fields.

```bash
lab guide | sed -n '/## Example/,/## Coordination/p' | head -60
lab schema | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin)['\$defs']['Test']; print(json.dumps(d,indent=1)[:1800])"
```

The baseline is one-hot position×amino-acid ridge with no biochemical features and no positional smoothing. I'll build a model with leakage-free target encoding of position (shrunk, with a ±2 window), mutant-AA effects, and physicochemical features, then compare it to the baseline with 5-fold CV on each dataset's train.csv before claiming anything.

The run failed because `lab exec` sets `EVAL_DIR` on every run, so the script took the prediction branch and found no dataset argument. I'll switch to explicit modes: `cv` for validation and `predict DATASET MODEL` for held-out inputs.

```bash
cd /work/dms
python3 - <<'EOF'
s = open('run.py').read()
s = s.replace("if EVAL is None:", "if sys.argv[1:2] != ['predict']:")
s = s.replace("ds_list = sys.argv[1:] or", "ds_list = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if a != 'cv'] or")
s = s.replace("ds = sys.argv[1]; model = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 'ens'",

The CV run is the evidence I need: the `hgb` arm beats the one-hot ridge baseline on mean MAE (0.227 vs 0.297) and on every one of the 7 datasets. Next I'll check that the `predict` path works under the evaluator's `EVAL_DIR` before I publish any prediction claims.


```bash
cd /work/dms
lab exec /work/dms -- python run.py predict BLAT_ECOLX_Stiffler_2015 hgb
```

The `predict` failure is expected here: `lab exec` sets `EVAL_DIR` to a location with no hidden inputs, so the evaluator will supply them later. To check the predict code path without touching evidence, I'll run it directly on a fake input file made from a slice of the training data.

```bash
cd /work/dms
mkdir -p /tmp/fake_eval/BLAT_ECOLX_Stiffler_2015 /tmp/fake_out
python3 -c "

The gain is consistent, so I'll test one method change before publishing more. The new feature is a per-position, per-amino-acid-class target mean (hydrophobic, polar, charged, Gly, Pro), shrunk toward the position mean. It is meant to capture position-specific substitution preferences that the current features miss.

Live checks passed for all 14 findings. I'll list the artifacts and budget to confirm the state, then close my part.
The run2 model is the best-supported result. I'll record the caveats (the 7 earlier findings are superseded, and all the claims share one method and one comparator) and then finish.

Founder summary: method = position target encoding (5-fold, shrunk, +/-2 window) + per-position amino-acid-class means + physicochemistry/BLOSUM62 + histogram gradient boosting (run2.py). Evidence: 5-fold CV on all 7 datasets (exec-f3c1cb30; mean MAE 0.220 vs 0.297 one-hot ridge) and an 80/20 holdout with the predict path (exec-fea6a840; mean MAE 0.215 vs 0.293, better than baseline on all 7). The 7 earlier run.py findings are superseded by the run2 set. All claims share one method and one comparator, so they are not independent replications. Not tested: the evaluator's own held-out variants.
